description.value: The study evaluated one sham-controlled right DLPFC HF-rTMS session and fifteen accelerated active HF-rTMS sessions on cue-induced alcohol craving and fMRI brain activation during block- and event-related alcohol cue exposure in recently detoxified alcohol-dependent patients.

spans.text: The current fMRI study consisted of 2 distinct research questions: an experimental part—evaluating one placebo-controlled HF-rTMS stimulation session—and an open label treatment part, consisting of fifteen accelerated active HF-rTMS sessions spread over 4 days.

value: Before stimulation, we expected that both cue-exposure paradigms would provoke immediate craving and elicit brain activation alterations especially in the craving neurocircuit.
For the sham-controlled single HF-rTMS session, we expected to find that only active and not sham HF-rTMS would suppress cue-induced craving.
Concerning the open-label treatment part, we expected that 15 HF-rTMS sessions would result in significant cue-induced and general craving reductions.

description.value: The experimental part was a randomized, sham-controlled, double-blind, between-subjects session; the treatment part was an open-label single-group accelerated active-stimulation study.
